Brexit shock

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Further information:
BREXIT SHOCK

No one really expected Britain to leave the EU. Even supporters of the leave campaign were shocked. David Cameron announced his resignation and uncertainty and volatility faces an already fragile global economy. Where to now? “ No one really knows” say the economists and anyone who tries to put numbers into the BREXIT equation are making things up.

For South Africa bumbling along on a less than 1% growth rate – its not good news either. Our currency already battered by dreadful internal policies is not likely to recover as investors run for certainty and abandon emerging markets. So what happened? Where did the anger come from and what happens next? Carte Blanche canvasses the views of two economists to see if and when there is any light for our beleaguered economy.

Press Release:


Brexit’s Shockwaves
No one really expected Britons to opt to leave the European Union. Even supporters of the leave campaign were stunned. Carte Blanche canvasses the views of top economists to gauge how hard South Africa’s sluggish economy will be hit by the Brexit shockwaves?


Script:


Brexit final script TX Sunday 3rd July 2016

Commentary One
With the sunrise came the shockwaves. As news reverberated from London’s epicenter that the UK had voted themselves out of the European Union. David Shapiro says even the bookies got it wrong

David Shapiro Director Sasfin Securities
We woke up to Friday morning absolutely broken and not sure how markets would react

Commentary Two
Then David Cameron announced his resignation.

Up sound David Cameron
We should aim to have a new pm in place by the start of the conservative party conference in October

Commentary Three
As the week progressed so did the anger and the divisions.

Up sound
We are European

Markets tanked, and Dr Thabi Leoka watched millions in value wiped out of the markets last Friday

Thabi Leoka
We saw about two trillion dollars lost in the equity markets including our JSE, the currency also weakened especially on the day about 7% still ebbing and flowing

Commentary four
Three trillion dollars later David Shapiro explains just why Brexit had such an impact

David Shapiro
The EU is about 22% of the global economy, America 25% China fifteen percent, so those are the big trading blocks! Within the EU, UK made up about 18 % and 20% so its big contributor, so when you tamper with EU, it spreads right through to the rest of the world. To give you an idea of SA we are .4% of the global economy. Africa is 2.4%

DEVI LINK
This is unchartered territory – and economists themselves are finding it difficult to call

Commentary five
Economist Dr Iraj Abedian



Dr Iraj
Brexit creates an episode against the evolution of civilization that is why we don’t know – that is why it wont be a quick thing or a constructive thing. I have absolutely no doubt this is a new lesson maybe painful we have to wait and see

Commentary Six
Here at home the last thing our embattled finance minister needed was Brexit

Iraj
Our growth in the last quarter contracted -1.2% and that was a shock by itself as far us as shocking in relative terms as Brexit. Our political and business leaders have a very limited window of opportunity to avoid SA being downgraded to junk status. Political leaders keep doing the wrong thing as if it doesn’t matter and the economy has been hammered into pulps.

David
We’ve been getting poorer for a long time now certainly over the last ten years. Every time the rand kicks we get poorer.
Devi
What do you see for interest rates?
David
They wont go up, you dare not, it would be absolutely disastrous
Devi
So what should government be doing?
David
Worrying. What we need to do is to start addressing issues that have nothing to do with Brexit – crime, corruption …those are the issues that make people not want to live here

Commentary seven
There have been warnings that Brexit could just be the beginning. So how do you survive the cold winds coming from the North

IRAJ
If you have property try to keep it, if you can get into property it’s a good thing to do

Thabi
Education, education, education. They should be more entrepreneurial. Everyone has to pull up their socks

DAVID
There is no prince Valiant coming to save you, you have to save yourself and the only way you can save yourself is to work harder and smarter and improve the skills you have


THE END


PROMO ONE 10 seconder
Anger and divisions in the UK, the prime minister resigns, three trillion dollars of value wiped off the markets, Brexit has shocked the world

PROMO TWO
The last thing our embattled finance minister needed was Brexit
Thabi Leoka
We saw about two trillion dollars lost in the equity markets including our JSE, the currency also weakened especially on the day about 7%

PROMO THREE
Brexit shockwaves are reverberating across the world
Iraj
If you have property keep it
David
No one is going to come and save you

Out at 00 05 01 00
